t: People of the 27th to 15th century BCE
cards: Hammurabi was a king of Babylon who reigned c. 1792–1750 BCE and built the Babylonian Empire across Mesopotamia.
r. c. 1792–1750 BCE · Ancient Near East
Thutmose III was a pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt and one of the most successful military rulers in its history.
Zimri-Lim was the last king of Mari, a city-state on the middle Euphrates in present-day Syria, in the eighteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1775–1761 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ur-Nammu was the founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, who established his rule around 2112 BCE after the collapse of the Akkadian Empire.
r. c. 2112–2094 BCE · Ancient Near East
Hattusili I was an early king of the Hittites, regarded as one of the founders of the Hittite kingdom.
r. c. 1650–1620 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ibbi-Sin was the last king of the Third Dynasty of Ur, reigning about 2028–2004 BCE.
r. c. 2028–2004 BCE · Ancient Near East
Samsu-iluna was king of Babylon and the son and successor of Hammurabi.
r. c. 1749–1712 BCE · Ancient Near East
Utu-hengal was a king of Uruk in the late 22nd century BCE who led the Sumerian cities against the Gutians.
r. c. 2120 BCE · Ancient Near East
Amenemhat III was a pharaoh of the Twelfth Dynasty who reigned for about 45 years in the 19th century BCE, the height of the Middle Kingdom.
r. c. 1831–1786 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Amenemhat IV was the penultimate king of the Twelfth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning for about nine years in the late nineteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1786–1777 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Enheduanna was the daughter of Sargon of Akkad, appointed high priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur.
fl. c. 2285–2250 BCE · Ancient Near East
Mentuhotep II was a king of the Theban Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt.
r. c. 2055–2004 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Rim-Sin I was a long-reigning king of Larsa in southern Mesopotamia and one of the most powerful rulers of the region in the early second millennium BCE.
r. c. 1822–1763 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ahmose I was the pharaoh who founded the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt around 1550 BCE.
r. c. 1550–1525 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Gudea was a ruler of the Sumerian city-state of Lagash around 2100 BCE, in the period between the fall of the Akkadian Empire and the rise of the Third Dynasty of Ur.
r. c. 2100 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ishbi-Erra was the founder of the First Dynasty of Isin, ruling about 2017–1985 BCE.
r. c. 2017–1985 BCE · Ancient Near East
Pepi II was a pharaoh of the Sixth Dynasty of Egypt, credited by tradition with one of the longest reigns in history, of up to 90 years.
r. c. 2278–2184 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Rimush was a king of the Akkadian Empire and a son and successor of Sargon of Akkad.
r. c. 2279–2270 BCE · Ancient Near East
Senusret III was a pharaoh of the Twelfth Dynasty of Middle Kingdom Egypt, reigning in the 19th century BCE.
r. c. 1878–1839 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Thutmose I was a pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt in the early New Kingdom.
r. c. 1506–1493 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Amenemhat I was the founder of Egypt's Twelfth Dynasty, reigning for about thirty years from around 1985 BCE.
c. 20th century BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Hatshepsut was a female pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt who ruled c. 1479–1458 BCE.
Khafre was a king of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty in the 26th century BCE and a son of Khufu.
Khufu was a king of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty in the 26th century BCE and the son of Sneferu.
Kindattu was a king of the Shimashki dynasty of Elam.
fl. c. 2004 BCE · Ancient Near East
Sneferu was the founder of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, reigning in the 26th century BCE.
Ur-Nanshe was the founder of the First Dynasty of Lagash in Sumer around 2500 BCE.
r. c. 2500 BCE · Ancient Near East
Yu the Great is the legendary Chinese ruler said to have tamed the great flood by dredging channels rather than building dams, and to have founded the Xia dynasty.
traditionally c. 2100 BCE · Central & East Asia
Enshakushanna was a king of Uruk in the Early Dynastic period, around the twenty-fourth century BCE, listed in the Sumerian King List.
c. 24th century BCE · Ancient Near East
Igrish-Halam was a king of Ebla in the twenty-fourth century BCE and one of the earliest rulers documented in the archives of its palace.
Khnumhotep II was a nomarch of the Oryx nome in Middle Egypt under the Twelfth Dynasty kings Amenemhat II and Senusret II.
Lugal-kinishe-dudu was a king of Uruk in the Early Dynastic period, around the twenty-fourth century BCE, who also ruled Ur and claimed kingship over both cities.
c. 24th century BCE · Ancient Near East
Manishtushu was a king of the Akkadian Empire in the twenty-third century BCE, a son of Sargon of Akkad.
r. c. 2270–2255 BCE · Ancient Near East
Mentuhotep III was a king of the Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt, son and successor of Mentuhotep II, who reigned about twelve years around 2000 BCE.
r. c. 2000 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Mentuhotep IV was the last king of the Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt, reigning for a few years around 1990 BCE and omitted from later king lists.
r. c. 1990 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Neferhotep I was a king of the Thirteenth Dynasty of Egypt who reigned for about eleven years in the mid-eighteenth century BCE, one of the best-attested rulers of the dynasty.
Senusret I was the second king of the Twelfth Dynasty of Egypt, son of Amenemhat I, reigning about 45 years in the twentieth century BCE.
Senusret II was a king of the Twelfth Dynasty of Egypt in the nineteenth century BCE.
Shu-Sin was the fourth king of the Third Dynasty of Ur, who reigned for about nine years in the late 21st century BCE.
r. c. 2037–2029 BCE · Ancient Near East
Sithathoriunet was an Egyptian princess of the Twelfth Dynasty, probably a daughter of Senusret II, buried near his pyramid at el-Lahun.
